text:
Situation: Sodium chloride injection is in short supply at multiple Corvale sites. Corvale East has 0.9 mg/mL 125 mL syringes at 10.2 days and 9 mg/mL at 9.2 days. Corvale General shows several sodium chloride entries ranging from 8.9 to 14.4 days. Corvale Lakeside has Sodium Chloride 9 mg/mL at 16.7 days. Sodium bicarbonate injection from Amphastar (posted 2017-03-01) and Exela (posted 2017-07-24) remains on FDA's shortage list, current as of 2026-10-21, for 140 months.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list shows sodium bicarbonate injection from Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc. posted 2017-03-01 and from Exela Pharma Sciences, LLC posted 2017-07-24, both still current as of 2026-10-21. FDA inspection records for plants on sodium chloride labels show multiple OAI classifications at Baxter Healthcare Corporation facilities, including inspections ending 2012-11-16, 2016-02-26, 2024-02-09, and 2026-04-02. FDA inspection records show OAI classifications at Hospira, Inc. facilities, including inspections ending 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, 2011-08-04, 2016-06-08, and 2018-08-15. FDA inspection records show OAI classifications at Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC facilities, including inspections ending 2011-07-08 and 2013-01-11.

Our position: Current sodium chloride inventory is below target days of supply at several locations. The rule-based best option is to buy from Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase orders for sodium chloride injection from Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer qualifies Medefil, Inc., Samson Medical Technologies, L.L.C., Sandoz Inc, and Sportpharm LLC as backup sources; requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer monitors daily usage and updates days-on-hand for all Corvale sites; requires pharmacy director approval.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative sodium-containing products without clinician and committee review.
